messages:
max: Quick follow-up from the RFC: we keep hitting weird latency spikes when a tenant crosses a residency threshold. Not full eviction, just a ~30-60ms tail bump. Anyone else seeing this pattern?

lina: Yep, saw it yesterday during the run with p99-sensitive routes. It correlates with slot reassignments and token-accounting drains.

raj: My hypothesis: the residency hysteresis currently uses a single timeout that triggers a compaction pass. That pass blocks the enqueue hot path for a few ms which cascades.

anya: Can you paste the compaction snippet? I remember we debated async vs sync compaction in the last RFC.

max: Here’s the simplified flow we have now:

```
if (tenant.queue_residency > RESIDENCY_LIMIT) {
  compact_inflight_sets_sync();  // may touch many queues
  mark_for_eviction();
}
```

lina: Right. The sync compaction is the issue. It scans a shard lock and yields. Even if compact is noop, the scan cost is nontrivial when many tiny queues exist.

raj: We could offload compaction to a background janitor and use a credit exchange to softly rebalance residency. Instead of immediate compaction we decrement a tenant's admission credits over time so they naturally yield.

anya: Soft-credit sounds promising. How would fairness be preserved vs a hard-preempt? I worry about starvation when a noisy tenant drains credits rapidly.

max: Two ideas: 1) Per-tenant token bucket that refills at a configured steady rate; 2) A fast-path borrow mechanism where a tenant can borrow a small burst if global headroom allows, but then pays back with extra cooldown.

raj: Borrowing plus cooldown maps well to leaky-bucket semantics. Pseudocode sketch:

```
credits = min(credits + refill(dt), max_credit)
if (credits >= req_cost) {
  allow_request(); credits -= req_cost;
} else if (global_headroom > borrow_threshold) {
  allow_request(); borrowed += req_cost; // tracked separately
  schedule_repay(borrowed, repay_window)
} else {
  queue_or_reject();
}
```

lina: That would avoid global scans. We still need a visibility mechanism: when many tenants borrow, we must degrade the fast-path. Maybe a simple moving average of borrowed across the node that triggers an admission slowdown.

anya: What about the KV cache pressure angle? Some of the tails align with massive KV evictions when compaction runs. If compaction is async, eviction still happens but staggered. We should couple credit-based residency with proactive cache pinning for p99 routes.

max: Good call. If a route is p99-sensitive we pin its recent prefixes, but pinning must honor memory budget. So credit bookkeeping should account for pin weight.

raj: Also, telemetry: we need fine-grained counters for: credit refill rate, borrow count, borrow repayment latency, compact duration, scan CPU. Ops needs these to correlate spikes.

lina: +1. Add an event that emits when a tenant hits soft-hysteresis (credit ~= 0) vs hard-eviction. Shifts in those event rates might predict tail spikes.

anya: Edge case: small ephemeral tenants (e.g., short-lived API keys) might never accumulate meaningful credit history. We should bootstrap them with a small grace credit on creation to avoid instant throttle.

max: Agreed. Implementation plan proposal:
- implement per-tenant token bucket with borrow accounting (non-blocking)
- move compaction to background janitor and make it cooperative (time-sliced)
- pinning hooks for flagged routes with memory budget enforcement
- telemetry + alerting (borrow rate > 5% -> inspect)

raj: Sounds good. For the janitor, prefer work-queue with per-shard soft-yield to avoid lock contention.

lina: One more: expose a route-level hedging knob that can opt into immediate evacuation for severe overloads (hard-preempt) — useful for critical tenants who bought guaranteed latency.

anya: Nice. That gives enterprise SLAs an escape hatch.

max: Ok I'll draft a short RFC addendum with proto APIs and metrics. Anyone want to own the prototype?

raj: I can prototype the token-bucket and borrow tracking this week.

lina: I’ll take the janitor refactor and the cooperative scan shim.

anya: I can do the pinning API and telemetry events.

sre-bot: NOTE: Deployment window required for changes touching admission/kvcache. Please schedule with eng-oncall and run canary on non-prod first. :white_check_mark:

max: Thanks all — assigning tasks in the RFC doc and will sync after prototypes. :thumbsup:
